Automatic cloud backup is turned off by default.
To copy a notebook to a USB drive, run northstar pack backup.nsb.
The pack file is a zip archive of the note text files.
Northstar does not encrypt the pack file.
Restore a pack file with northstar unpack backup.nsb.

# Commands

List every note in the current notebook with northstar list.
The list is sorted by the time the note was last modified, newest first.
Add a note titled Week 3 with northstar add "Week 3". You will be prompted to type the body. Save the note by entering a line that contains only a period.
Search note bodies with northstar search followed by a word, for example northstar search mitochondria. Search is case-insensitive and matches whole words only. It does not search titles.

# Getting started

Northstar Notes is a command-line notebook for course work. Each note is stored as its own plain text file.
Install Northstar Notes with pip: pip install northstar-notes. The version described in this documentation is 2.4.1.
You need Python 3.10 or newer before you install Northstar Notes. Older Python versions are not supported.
Create a notebook named lab-journal with northstar init lab-journal. That command creates a folder called lab-journal and a file named notebook.toml inside it.

Limits

Note size

The maximum note body is 20000 characters. Longer notes are rejected with the error NOTE_TOO_LONG.

Capacity

A notebook may contain at most 500 notes. Creating another note after that fails.

Export

Export to PDF with the command northstar export pdf. Export to HTML is not available.

# Storage

By default, notebooks live in a folder named Northstar inside your home directory.
Each note is a UTF-8 text file. The file name is the note title with spaces replaced by hyphens, followed by the .txt extension.
Northstar never stores notes in a database. If you delete a .txt file from the notebook folder, the note is gone.
Attachments are not supported. A note may contain only text.
